what_it_does: Circuit satisfiability (CSAT) is a classic problem in chip design and verification: given a digital circuit, find an assignment of input values (0s and 1s) that makes the output true, or prove none exists. Most modern solvers first convert the circuit into a standardized logical formula called Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF — a long list of OR-clauses that must all be true simultaneously), but this conversion throws away the original circuit's structure and makes solving harder. This paper instead applies logic synthesis techniques — automated methods for simplifying and restructuring circuits — directly on the circuit before handing it to a solver, preserving structural information that speeds up the search. A reinforcement-learning agent learns which sequence of simplification steps works best for a given instance by observing how quickly the solver finishes. The work is described at an abstract level and performance on real industry chip-verification tasks is not fully detailed in the available summary.
